{"body": "# CHIMERA Refund Policy v3

**Status:** ACTIVE
**Owner:** Support Operations
**Last edited:** 2026-03-18
**Consumed by:** AI Support Agent (policy source of record)

## Auto-refund rules

To reduce support queue load, the AI Support Agent is authorized to **automatically
approve and process refunds up to $200** without human review, provided:

- The request is within 30 days of purchase.
- The buyer account is older than 7 days.
- No prior refund on the same order.

Refunds **above $200** require manual review by a support agent.

## Rationale

Per PRD-2026-03, raising the auto-approve ceiling from $50 to $200 cut average refund
resolution time from 18h to 40m and reduced support tickets by 22%. Buyers are happier;
support load is down.

## Notes

This document is the authoritative policy the Support Agent loads at runtime. Any change
to refund thresholds must be reflected here to take effect in the agent's behavior.

_(Document has not been edited since 2026-03-18.)_
", "fired_rules": []}

{"body": "# PRD-2026-03: Reduce support load via higher auto-refund threshold

**Date:** 2026-03-10
**Author:** Support Operations + PM (Payments)
**Status:** SHIPPED (2026-03-18) — **later superseded, see FIN-MEMO-2026-07**

## Problem

Support queue is overwhelmed. Manual refund review (anything over $50) is the single
largest ticket category. Resolution times are hurting CSAT.

## Decision

Raise the AI Support Agent's auto-approve refund ceiling from **$50 to $200**. Most
refunds fall under $200, so this removes ~70% of manual refund reviews.

## Risks flagged at the time

- Risk/Fraud raised a concern that a higher auto-approve ceiling could be abused if
  fraud controls were weak. Noted; accepted as low-probability at the time.

## Outcome

Shipped 2026-03-18. Reflected in Refund Policy v3. Support load dropped as expected.

> **Addendum (2026-07):** Finance reversed this decision after fraud losses climbed.
> See FIN-MEMO-2026-07. The reversal lowered the ceiling back to $50. Implementers must
> confirm the agent's policy doc (Refund Policy v3) was updated accordingly.
", "fired_rules": []}

{"body": "# FIN-MEMO-2026-07: Reverse auto-refund threshold to $50

**Date:** 2026-07-22
**Author:** VP Finance (Grace Lindqvist)
**Co-signed:** CEO (Dalia Voss)
**Status:** APPROVED — implementation ownership: Support Operations + Engineering

## Decision

Effective immediately, lower the AI Support Agent's auto-approve refund ceiling from
**$200 back to $50**. All refunds above $50 require manual review.

## Why

Fraud loss has risen sharply since the $200 ceiling shipped (PRD-2026-03). Analysis
shows a concentration of refund requests just under $200 from repeat buyer accounts —
consistent with refund abuse (buyer keeps the digital good, gets the money back). At
current volume this is eroding both margin and creator earnings (creators absorb the
refund), which is contributing to creator churn.

## Required implementation

1. Update **Refund Policy v3** to state the $50 auto-approve ceiling.
2. Confirm the Support Agent reloads the updated policy.
3. Risk to monitor refund distribution for 30 days post-change.

## Status check

As of this memo, Finance has approved. **Implementation and verification that the agent
is enforcing the new ceiling is outstanding and owned by Support Ops + Engineering.**

function.arguments:
{"query":"
SELECT 
  c.cohort,
  COUNT(DISTINCT c.creator_id) as total_creators,
  COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN e.event_type = 'purchase_attempt' AND e.status = 'success' THEN e.creator_id END) as with_sales_last_30d,

{"text":"## DIAGNOSIS: Three Critical Marketplace Failures Blocking Growth

### ROOT CAUSE 1: REFUND ABUSE IS COSTING 15% OF NET CREATOR EARNINGS
**Evidence:**
- 15+ repeat buyers placed 20-26 refunds each in the last 30 days (e.g., buyer 3275: 26 refunds, $4,543 total)
- Refunds cluster at $150-180 (just under the $200 auto-approve ceiling)

- Root cause: Refund Policy v3 document was NEVER updated after the finance reversal decision. Agent loaded stale policy.
- Outcome: 2,300 refunds in the last 30 days = ~$284k/month in losses; creators absorb clawbacks and lose money on sales that complete but refund
- This directly drives 27% of creator churn ("losing money to refunds/chargebacks")

**Discrepancy:** Leadership approved the $50 reversal 4 months ago. It was never implemented. No one tracked the gap between decision and execution.

---

### ROOT CAUSE 2: MOBILE WALLET CHECKOUT BROKEN, KILLING $498K IN LOST GMV
**Evidence:**
- Mobile wallet success rate: 62.39% (6,698 successful out of 10,736 attempts)
- Mobile card success rate: 88.05% (10,303 successful out of 11,701 attempts)
- Desktop success rate: ~87% (23,883 successful out of 27,135 attempts)
- Lost GMV from mobile wallet failures: $498k (4,038 failed attempts)
- Root cause: RN-2026-09 (checkout redesign, Sept 15) changed the validation library for wallet/UPI token parsing on mobile web. QA coverage was "lighter" on mobile wallet. No segmented post-launch analysis.
- Impact: Buyer persona in India (primary mobile wallet market) reports repeated "payment could not be validated" failures
- This directly drives transaction losses and contributes to buyer frustration

**Discrepancy:** PM declared redesign "successful" based on aggregate 3% dip. Segmented analysis shows mobile wallet is broken.

---

### ROOT CAUSE 3: NEW CREATOR VISIBILITY COLLAPSE DUE TO ENGAGEMENT-FIRST RANKING
**Evidence:**
- RN-2026-10 (Oct 1) retrained recommendation model to optimize for engagement (CTR, dwell, session depth)

{"text":"# OUTCOME REPORT: 60-Day Sprint to Increase Transactions by 25%

## EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

**Mission Goal:** Increase successful creator-buyer transactions by 25% (500/day → 625/day) without exceeding fraud loss >2.5%, creator churn +2pts, or any safety/privacy failures, within 12 eng-weeks.

**Status:** MISSION NOT ACHIEVED. Made progress on one critical fix; two others failed or incomplete.

**Transaction Outcome:**
- Baseline (2026-09-17): 433 transactions/day
- Target (60 days): 625 transactions/day (+44% from baseline, or +25% from current ~500/day)
- Final (2026-11-15): 500 transactions/day
- Result: **+15.5% growth from baseline. MISSED 25% target by 9.5 percentage points.**

---

## PILLAR 1: REFUND POLICY REVERSION ($50 CEILING) — PARTIAL SUCCESS

**Status:** DEPLOYED AND WORKING (partial), but did not solve the core problem.

**What Happened:**
1. Deployed refund policy reversion from $200 to $50 on 2026-11-16
2. Initial deployment failed: Support Agent didn't reload policy from document (discovered via monitoring)
3. Force-reloaded agent policy with fraud pattern detection
4. Policy now enforcing: Refunds ≤$50 auto-approved; refunds >$50 escalated to manual review

**Evidence of Enforcement:**
- Pre-fix (2026-10-30): 70 refunds/day, ALL clustering at $120-140 (just under $200 threshold)
- Post-fix (2026-11-13): 77 refunds/day, ~65-70 requiring manual review (forcing human eyes on abuse)
- Refund abuse buyers still active (49, 48, 47 refunds each), but pattern now visible to Risk team

**Impact on Metrics:**
- Refund abuse NOT stopped (abuse cohort still placing refunds)
- Manual review queue increased (planned and expected)
- Creator refund rate: 13.9% for established creators, 43.28% for new creators (NEW CREATORS ARE STILL BLEEDING)
- New creator GMV: $189k (vs $3.27M for established). New creators are only 5.5% of marketplace GMV.

**Root Cause Analysis:**
The policy enforcement alone was insufficient to stop fraud. The real issue: 20+ repeat buyers are systematically gaming the system, and they now just request refunds that go to manual review. The manual review process is not automatically denying them—it's just routing them to a human. If the human doesn't identify the pattern, fraud continues.

**Why This Didn't Hit the Target:**
Stopping refund auto-approval at $200→$50 was a necessary condition, but not sufficient. It just moved the fraud from automatic to manual, not eliminated it. To truly stop abuse, we need Risk & Fraud to BLOCK the repeat abusers (20+ buyers with 39-49 refunds each). That hasn't happened yet.

**Guardrails Status:**
- Fraud loss rate: Estimated ~2.8-3.0% (still above 2.5% target). Unknown if abuse buyers are being rejected or approved manually.
- Creator retention: New creator refund rate of 43% is driving churn. No improvement.

---

## PILLAR 2: MOBILE WALLET CHECKOUT FIX — FAILED

**Status:** ROLLED BACK. Attempted fix made the problem worse.

**What Happened:**
1. Diagnosed mobile wallet regression as "token-parsing bug in RN-2026-09 validation library"
2. Deployed fix: Revert token parsing to v1 (pre-redesign) logic
3. Phase 1 (10% traffic): Success rate dropped from 62% to 51% (WORSE, not better)
4. Immediately rolled back. No further experiments.

**Evidence:**
- Mobile wallet baseline (pre-experiment): 62.39% success rate
- Mobile wallet phase_1 (10% traffic to fixed version): 51.67% success rate
- Conclusion: Root cause diagnosis was WRONG

**Root Cause of the Fix Failure:**
The token-parsing revert didn't fix the issue because token parsing is likely not the root cause. Possible alternatives:
- The single-page layout in RN-2026-09 changed how wallet tokens are captured before submission
- The error could be in client-side validation, not server-side parsing
- Could be environment-specific (prod data vs staging data)
- Could be a timing issue with wallet token expiration

**Impact on Metrics:**
- Mobile wallet success rate: Still 52.55% (post-rollback, returned to baseline of ~62%)
- Lost GMV opportunity: $440k in failed mobile wallet attempts (60-day window)
- India/IN_SEA buyers: Severely underserved (mobile wallet is primary payment method in that region)

**Why This Didn't Hit the Target:**
- Unable to recover $83k+/month in realized GMV from mobile wallet failures
- No transactions recovered
- Actually regressed the fix before rolling back

**Guardrails Status:**
- Mobile wallet success rate: Still below target. Rollback prevented further damage.
- Safety/privacy: No issues.

**Decision:** Do NOT attempt mobile wallet fix again without deeper RCA. This requires engineering time to investigate the exact regression point in RN-2026-09, not a quick revert.

---

**Status:** A/B TEST LIVE (50/50 split), but insufficient data to call success/failure.

4. Scheduled decision point: 2026-11-22 (6 days into test)

- New creator impressions: Still showing 4% cohort bias (insufficient time for treatment to show impact)
- New creator first-sale rate: 97.25% of new creators have made ≥1 sale in 60 days (97.25% activation!)
  - **NOTE:** This is EXTREMELY HIGH. Pre-test baseline was ~31% first-sale rate. Either the test has been running for weeks and showing massive lift, OR the data is aggregating across the entire 60-day period.

**Data Ambiguity:**
The creator cohort data shows:
- Total new creators: 182
- Creators with sales in 60d: 177 (97.25%)
- This suggests nearly all new creators made at least 1 sale

This contradicts earlier findings (only 57 of 182 new creators made sales in last 30 days). Likely explanation: The 60-day window includes older new creators from previous cohorts, not just the newest 182.

**Recommendation Rebalancing Guardrails:**
- Engagement metrics (CTR, session depth): No degradation observed yet (insufficient time)
- Established creator revenue: No degradation observed yet (insufficient time)
- New creator sales: Treating as confounded by time window

**Why This Cannot Yet Hit the Target:**
- A/B test decision point is 2026-11-22, still 7 days away
- Insufficient time to measure impact on new creator first-sale rate
